items.title: Virginia Mayhew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2022
items.q: And the next time it was a quartet with — who did I take — Harvie S., Allison Miller and Daniel Kelley on piano.

ctx.x: Yup. The first time it was a trio, Allison Miller and Gary Wang. And the next time it was a quartet with — who did I take — Harvie S., Allison Miller and Daniel Kelley on piano. It was just — that was bossa nova. The first one the theme was Louis Armstrong, the second one the theme was bossa nova, or something, what was it — I think it was bossa nova or something like that. And it was just really, it was so much fun and people just loved it and it was just such an amazing experience to see all these…

Let’s talk about Al Grey for a minute. He was one of the first people we interviewed way back in ’95, and then a couple of years later I happened to go to Sweet Basil’s and he was playing there. And he played this tune called “Echoes of New Orleans.” It was so catchy. And afterwards I went up to him and I said, “Mr. Grey, that is the coolest tune.” And he goes, “Yeah, I got a hit!” And I thought that’s so cool that this guy, that he was probably in his late 70s at least, and that he had a hit.
